newsitem.title: USA: New York housewives held in drug trafficking ring.
newsitem.headline: New York housewives held in drug trafficking ring.

text.p: A group of suburban housewives posing as tourists allegedly smuggled hundreds of thousands of dollars' worth of heroin and cocaine between the United States, Europe and South America, U.S. officials said on Thursday.

The New York office of the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) said five women from Long Island were among 14 people arrested so far in a two-year undercover probe of the sophisticated international drug-trafficking operation.

"We have seen similar unstereotypical methods used in the past but not to this extent -- involving middle-class women who acted as couriers and were careful not to make too many trips that would reveal a pattern," said DEA special agent Robin Waugh.

She said the women were trying to "make a quick buck" from cocaine that sells for an estimated $50,000 a kilogram, or about 2.2 pounds, in Europe and $22,000 a kilogram in the United States. Some of the heroin carried by the women had an estimated street value in the hundreds of thousands of dollars.

Waugh said the housewives made an estimated two or three trips a year, picking up the drugs in South America on journeys that saw them glide through customs in Quito, the capital of Ecuador, Buenos Aires, Rio de Janiero, Rome, Istanbul, Bucharest and New York.

Four of the alleged ringleaders, identified as Lonnie Lee Lloyd, Sherman Tucker, Al Grimes and Willie Grimes, were indicted on Thursday on cocaine and heroin trafficking charges in U.S. District Court in the Eastern District of New York. Another man was arraigned on cocaine and heroin trafficking charges in the same district on Thursday.

"The men played a double role as the organisers and recruiters of the operation, while the women acted as the couriers," Waugh said. "We used undercover agents as well as physical and electronic surveillance methods in our investigation."
Waugh said the DEA's initial probe began in March 1995 after the agency was alerted by an informant. The ring was allegedly started by six former U.S. Navy men who had served together in Italy.
